items.headline: Lakefront offloads CAR-T programs to Armed Cell as Mankind Pharma takes control
items.preview: Lakefront Biotherapeutics has sold five preclinical CAR-T assets to Armed Cell for €8 million upfront.
items.article:
Lakefront Biotherapeutics has sold five preclinical CAR-T assets to Belgian startup Armed Cell Therapeutics for €8 million upfront, while India's Mankind Pharma has agreed to acquire 70% of Armed Cell for €48 million.
Why this matters: This sale allows the cancer cell-therapy research that Lakefront was shutting down to continue with new financing, while Lakefront focuses on a new pipeline in immunology and inflammation.
Under the deal, Lakefront could receive up to $230 million in milestones and a low-single-digit royalty in addition to the upfront payment. Armed Cell aims to advance its lead programs into clinical trials with the new funding.

items.headline: Printing Tissue in Orbit: How Space Is Becoming the Next Biomedical Lab
items.preview: A new review highlights how microgravity can enhance tissue engineering and biomedical research.
items.article:
Researchers at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center argue that space could be a powerful tool for biomedicine, enabling tissue fabrication and disease modeling in microgravity.
Why this matters: The unique conditions of space can help create human tissues that are difficult to construct on Earth, providing insights into aging and degenerative diseases.
The review discusses advancements in tissue engineering, 3D bioprinting, and biosensors that could revolutionize biomedical research in space, potentially leading to faster drug development and better understanding of human health.

items.headline: Biogen-backed Estuary nabs $93M for kidney disease gene therapy
items.preview: Estuary Biotherapeutics has launched with $93 million in funding to develop gene therapies for kidney disease.
items.article:
Estuary Biotherapeutics, a California-based genetic medicines developer, has officially launched with significant funding and a team of former Biogen leaders.
Why this matters: The company aims to develop the first treatment that can halt or reverse autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), a condition affecting 1 in 400 to 1,000 people. Their lead programs target the main drivers of ADPKD and are expected to enter human testing in 2027 and 2028.

items.headline: FDA ‘reset’ continues with new plan for reviewing rare disease drugs
items.preview: The FDA plans to overhaul its approach to regulating therapies for rare diseases.
items.article:
The FDA announced its intention to 'reimagine' the regulation of therapies for rare diseases, focusing on individual conditions rather than a one-size-fits-all approach.
Why this matters: This initiative aims to create a more tailored framework for drug development and regulation, potentially easing the path for new treatments for rare diseases, which affect approximately 30 million Americans. A meeting to gather feedback on this plan is scheduled for October 28.

items.headline: A broad-host-range Rhizobium rhizogenes strain enables transient expression across diverse crop species
items.preview: A new engineered strain of Rhizobium rhizogenes facilitates transient expression in various dicot crops.
items.article:
An engineered Rhizobium rhizogenes strain, AS109, has been shown to mediate efficient transient expression across diverse dicot species, outperforming traditional agrobacterial strains.
Why this matters: This advancement provides a versatile platform for functional genomics in non-model crops, bridging the gap between hypothesis generation and experimental validation in plant research. The study demonstrates AS109's effectiveness in various economically important crops, enhancing research capabilities in plant biology.
